verification.acceptance: A scenario naming any capability present in contracts/pulse-capabilities.toml validates at load; one absent from it is rejected with a message naming the manifest rather than a hardcoded range; a malformed, absent or unparseable manifest produces a typed harness fault carrying a named reason — never a silent widen back to a hardcoded range, never a silent pass, never a panic. capabilities.title: SUT-drift check
capabilities.requirement: A check fails loudly when the SUT advances past what Conductor knows, rather than silently accepting a stale capability universe.
capabilities.observed_gap: Nothing in the repo detects that Pulse has advanced: the accepted set is a compile-time constant and the coverage universe is frozen, so 22 new Pulse capabilities (P-061..P-082) went unnoticed across a 41-day pause.

verification.acceptance: When the manifest carries capabilities the classification does not cover beyond an explicitly pinned known-gap ledger, the check fails naming the unknown ids; when the observed gap matches the pin exactly — and no classified row lacks manifest backing — it passes. A pinned id that has since been classified is itself a failure, so the ledger cannot rot. With an empty pin the check is a plain zero-drift assertion, proven by test in this chunk and the state v2-03 leaves it in.

capabilities.title: SUT load-envelope constraint
capabilities.requirement: Scenario durations and storm profiles stay inside the SUT's proven-good envelope, with the constraint recorded where scenario authors will see it.
capabilities.observed_gap: Pulse records that the DuckDB append path stalls after ~10 minutes of sustained 10k/s storm plus deterministic L4 — ingest keeps receiving while duckdb.append stops, so viz.query.traces returns 0 rows and no new incidents form until restart. Conductor's whole method is sustained shaped load.

verification.acceptance: `check_load_envelope` asserts, for every scenario in the committed catalog, that no emitting phase exceeds `max_sustained_storm_ms` and no emitting phase's rate (`occurrences / (gap_ms/1000)`) exceeds `max_sustained_rate_spans_per_s`, with the `[[exempt]]` ledger EMPTY and still held to exact-set equality in all three directions (`unpinned`/`rotted`/`lost_subject`); `LoadEnvelope::classify` judges a run on the same basis, so the static gate and the per-run judgment never measure different things; and the bounds stay recorded in `contracts/pulse-load-envelope.toml` with the per-scenario LOAD ENVELOPE header present in all 35 `scenarios/*.toml`. Proven by `cargo nextest run -p conductor-core`.

capabilities.notes: PREMISE-CORRECTION (2026-08-13, phase P3 research). `contracts/pulse-load-envelope.toml:40-42` and the working-route CARRY both recorded that asserting SUMMED emitting-phase duration would let both `[[exempt]]` entries retire on their own merits. Measured across all 35 committed scenarios against the 600000 ms ceiling, both remain over on that basis (activity-floor 900000, incident-auto-resolution 610000), so the summed re-scope is a no-op on the gate's verdict and retiring the exemptions under it would turn the gate red. Cause: activity-floor's three train-active phases are 300000 ms each and genuinely emit, but are separated by 10-minute quiets -- summing disjoint bursts is not 'sustained', which is what its own exemption reason said. Resolved by asserting the envelope's own prose instead: a PER-PHASE joint bound (sustained-storm duration + rate). Catalog-wide the longest single emitting phase is 600000 ms (exactly at the ceiling, not over) and the highest per-phase rate is 4.00 spans/s against the 10000 spans/s term, so zero phases breach and the ledger genuinely retires to []. Operator-approved at the phase P5 review. The acceptance above is the normal claim-exit concretization of the standing outcome, not an absorption of the disproved premise -- the outcome text itself was never falsified. Evidence: conductor-0.2.0/chunks/2026-08-13-dispatcher-determinism-goldens/research.md (Open questions 1) and conductor-0.2.0/chunks/2026-08-13-dispatcher-determinism-goldens/scope.md (PREMISE-CORRECTION).

Two prior chunks declined this claim; both declines were honest and both are now superseded by measurement. NOTES RE-BASED on the 2026-08-16 legs: the 'second independent unknown' the prior decline recorded (the storm's 12 distinct-seeded-id spans appending zero rows) is RESOLVED — with the constant-span-identity fix in place the appender is healthy, measured as 27 duckdb.append lines with ZERO reject_reason, rows_ingested 15 and the buffer.tick trio at 12/12/12; the earlier zero-append reading was a downstream effect of the same primary-key collision, not a separate defect. The gate was re-aimed onto incident freshness (opened_at_unix_nano, sourced from the corpus row's created_unix_nano at mcp-server/tools.rs:412, compared against a std::time emission stamp) and reached ready:true, canary_round_trip ok, exit 0. capabilities.notes: 2026-08-14-canary-fingerprint-feed-capture DECLINED this cap and it stays pooled: that chunk diagnoses why Pulse's storm detector tracked zero fingerprints, which is answerable without an incident, while this acceptance needs the family scenarios driven end-to-end and read back through MCP — an incident Pulse's 3,600s-per-service BootstrapState::Ready gate still prevents. The chunk partially advances the cap by removing the fingerprint-feed blocker and is cited in its plan.md provenance. Evidence carried forward for the next claiming chunk: Pulse's tracked_fingerprints_count is a 60s-windowed gauge over DISTINCT fingerprints sampled every 15s after eviction, so a working six-occurrence identical-fingerprint storm reads 1, never 6 — do not author an acceptance expecting 6. The latched discriminators are storms_detected_total and fingerprints_evicted_total on the same tick line; both read 0 across every sample of the three-arm probe, including a tick postdating arm 3's entire canary window. 2026-08-16-fingerprint-storm-live-proof CLAIMS this cap and concretized the acceptance at phase P5. Two concretization facts worth recording. (a) The scenario as previously authored could not prove the outcome: under the shipped blake3 derivation PathVariant diverged, so the declared triple produced TWO fingerprints, neither phase boundary landed where its name claimed, and the path fingerprint raised an unnamed second Suggested cue. The chunk re-shapes PathVariant to an ABSOLUTE-path change (stripped by normalize_frame) so the triple genuinely shares one fingerprint, with a new RelativePath member carrying the relative-path significance the reshape retires. (b) The acceptance's distinctness clause lives in a SECOND scenario (fingerprint-distinct.toml), so the leg drives both rather than demoting that half to unit tier — operator decision at the phase P5 review. PREMISE-CORRECTION (2026-08-16, measured on the live legs): this acceptance's ">60s separation" clause is INSUFFICIENT on its own for same-dir back-to-back legs. It is correct about Pulse's 60s storm-retention window, but a second independent mechanism also blocks a second leg — Pulse dedupes a new incident against any OPEN incident and NOT by fingerprint (the canary's exception_type is ConductorCanary_{now_ms}, unique per run and therefore a distinct fingerprint, and it deduped anyway), so the first storm leg returned Blocked with 'no incident opened after the canary storm was emitted'. On a shared dir the only cure is auto-resolve at roughly five minutes; the graded re-run used a FRESH DATA DIR PER LEG, which dissolves both hazards. The acceptance text stands; this records what it under-specified. The dedupe semantics are a Pulse product-design question (Pulse-visit candidate #4), not a Conductor defect. Also measured: retrieve_report returns degraded_mode:true PERMANENTLY under deterministic L4, so the scenarios' Contains/Absent 'RetryStorm' read-back checks were structurally ungradeable (the Absent side passed vacuously); they are retired to declare-only and their assertions moved to the harvest surface, and slo_tier was re-calibrated <20s -> <90s because latency_ms spans the scenario's own ~24s/~30s emission window. Both were performed under this acceptance's own re-calibration clause.

capabilities.title: Workspace-key divergence detected
capabilities.requirement: Conductor detects an app/sidecar workspace-key mismatch and fails with a named precondition rather than an opaque Blocked; the real fix stays Pulse-side.
capabilities.observed_gap: Incidents are filtered WHERE workspace = ?1; pulse-app derives that key via resolve_workspace_for_incidents (the detected project root) while the sidecar always uses data_dir, so if pulse-app launches anywhere the detector recognises, query_incident_list returns zero rows and preflight reports the opaque Blocked: incident not found in corpus even with deterministic L4 on.

verification.acceptance: A simulated app/sidecar key mismatch (the stub's empty-corpus arm — a diverged key and an empty corpus are byte-identical on the wire) produces a distinct named precondition, not the generic corpus Blocked, returned as Ok(Blocked); the precondition string carries no absolute host path; and a fingerprint-miss leg proves the two not-found causes stay distinguishable. The live launch probe is run once across three arms — cwd = the Conductor repo root, cwd = a marker-less temp dir, cwd = the data dir itself — with each arm's ready and blocked_precondition recorded in the chunk's two-launch-verdict.md.

capabilities.notes: PREMISE-CORRECTION (2026-08-10, chunk 2026-08-10-workspace-key-divergence-probe). CONFIRMED first-hand against the Pulse source: incidents filter WHERE workspace = ?1 (crates/corpus/src/contract.rs:628); pulse-app keys on the detected root via resolve_workspace_for_incidents (pulse-app/src/main.rs:688-693 -> digest_runtime.rs:109-127); the sidecar keys on data_dir (crates/mcp-server/src/bin/andromeda-pulse-mcp.rs:74, under a parity comment stale since Pulse's P-079). FALSIFIED: the premise that a marker-less temp dir makes pulse-app fall back to data_dir. workspace_detector::detect (crates/workspace-detector/src/detect.rs:21-57) records the .andromeda marker and VCS as FIELDS on the returned context, not success conditions, and errors only on a traversal component or a non-existent path — so detection succeeds for virtually any real cwd, a marker-less temp dir keys to that temp dir, and the data_dir fallback is effectively unreachable from a normal launch. Consequences: no cwd-based interim unblock is known to exist, and the probe gains a third arm (cwd == the data dir — the only position where the two keys could agree, itself in doubt because Windows canonicalize returns the \\?\ verbatim prefix while the sidecar uses the raw data_dir string). ALSO ESTABLISHED: Conductor cannot OBSERVE the app-side key — dispatch_query_incident_list takes no arguments (crates/mcp-server/src/tools.rs:174,336), Pulse never logs incident_workspace_key, and corpus.db is out of bounds by rule — so the deliverable is a named precondition stating the condition and both candidate causes, never a claimed measurement. intent.md and requirements.md are immutable records of what was ASKED and are deliberately unedited; this ledger entry is the correction channel.

capabilities.title: Machine-checked Pulse run contract
capabilities.requirement: A recorded, reproducible run contract that preflight asserts and whose unmet terms it names; doubles as the verification of Pulse P-073.
capabilities.observed_gap: Nothing in this repo states how a verifiable Pulse must be launched; conductor-verify/src/spawn.rs:18 passes only ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR, and there are zero references to Pulse's deterministic mode anywhere in the tree.

verification.acceptance: Preflight asserts the contract terms — ANDROMEDA_PULSE_L4_DETERMINISTIC set on the launched pulse-app (not the sidecar) and both sides resolving the same data dir — and names each unmet term individually; the contract is recorded in-repo and reproducible.

capabilities.notes: PREMISE-CORRECTION (2026-08-10, chunk 2026-08-10-pulse-run-contract). The acceptance prose reads as though preflight ASSERTS both named terms. Only one is assertable, and the acceptance text is deliberately left unedited as the record of what was ASKED. WHAT IS ASSERTED: ANDROMEDA_PULSE_L4_DETERMINISTIC, through a shell-declaration proxy — Conductor reads its OWN environment, the shell that also launches pulse-app — shipped as check = "shell-declaration" in contracts/pulse-run-contract.toml, the only check kind that can block. WHAT IS NOT: 'both sides resolving the same data dir'. Conductor propagates its resolved data dir to the sidecar via the .env(...) builder, so the sidecar half is guaranteed by construction, but pulse-app's half is structurally unobservable — the exact limit v2-17's notes established, since dispatch_query_incident_list takes no arguments (crates/mcp-server/src/tools.rs:174,336), Pulse never logs the incident workspace key, and corpus.db is out of bounds by rule. That term therefore ships as check = "declared-not-observable" with its causes recorded: it is stated so an operator can satisfy it, and it never blocks, because blocking on it would assert a measurement Conductor cannot make. CONSEQUENCE: 'preflight asserts the contract terms' holds for every term Conductor can honestly observe, and the artifact itself carries the distinction per-term rather than leaving a reader to infer it. The coverage flip stands on the refs, not on the prose. Same channel as v2-17: intent.md and requirements.md are immutable records of what was asked and are deliberately unedited; this ledger entry is the correction channel.

capabilities.notes: PREMISE-CORRECTION (2026-08-10, chunk 2026-08-10-scenario-run-root-span-tree). The acceptance prose reads as though the report and db spans can be NESTED BENEATH the scenario.run root. They cannot, and the acceptance text is deliberately left unedited as the record of what was ASKED. WHAT IS ACHIEVABLE: scenario.run is per-scenario at the composition root (conductor-run::execute_scenario, lib.rs:253), parenting timeline.execute, emit.batch and verify.readback* -- one instrumentation site serving all three production paths. WHAT IS NOT: report.generate and db.insert_run nested beneath that root. The code-graph shows persist() is a SIBLING of execute_scenario, called by execute_scenario's own callers at all three production sites -- conductor-cli commands/run/run() (run.rs:23 execute, :25 persist), conductor-cli commands/suite/suite() (suite.rs:30 execute, :36 persist), and conductor-run drive_run() (lib.rs:481 execute, :485 persist, plus a second persist at :478 on the abort path). Under suite and drive_run a SINGLE persist serves N scenarios whose spans have already closed, so no one scenario.run can contain db.insert_run. The two terminal spans are therefore emitted at the persist boundary and correlated by run_id, which the subscriber layer already stamps flat on every line (obs.rs:265-268). ALSO CORRECTED: the observed_gap says the must-trace paths have 'leaf spans with no root correlation'. Verified at P3 that the shipped spans emit NOTHING -- JsonObsLayer (obs.rs:239-276) implements only on_event, never on_new_span/on_close, and binds its Context as unused _ctx; the committed logs/agent-latest.jsonl contains 0 occurrences of timeline.execute, emit.batch or verify.readback. The gap was not missing correlation but missing span emission entirely, which is why this chunk also lands the subscriber-layer capability and widens the conductor-core::redact allowlist (row_count, phase_count, emission_count, record_count, mcp_tool would otherwise be dropped at the processor stage). CHANNEL: note-only, matching v2-18's treatment at 2026-08-10-pulse-run-contract. Refining the acceptance text was considered and rejected -- the only sanctioned acceptance-refinement class today is affordance honesty; 'premise disproved' is a proposed second class awaiting the founder's P6 ruling, at which point v2-18 and v2-31 take the same retroactive treatment under one rule. The coverage flip stands on the ref proving the achievable shape.
